correctness.rationale: Conjugating by H^(1/2) reduces exact line minimization to rank-one orthogonal projections. Reflection removes off-diagonal expectations. With t=√κ, W=t²/(t²+X²) for standard Cauchy X satisfies EW=t/(t+1) and E[W(1−W)]=t/[2(t+1)²] by differentiation. In the independent case conditioning on the first direction gives diag(t²+t+2,t(2t²+t+1))/(2(t+1)³). For the paired case I checked the printed partial fraction and both overlap moments symbolically via a two-parameter Cauchy resolvent and differentiation before substituting the reciprocal parameter (/workspace/independent_checks.py). These give precisely the stated scalar multiple of the independent matrix. Its second diagonal entry is largest since the unnormalized difference is 2(t³−1); both bounds are attained on the smaller-eigenvalue mode. At t=1 the paired projections are complementary and the iid result is 1/4; at t=2 the factors are 11/27 and 11/75. The statement about not preserving first-line optimality is generic, not a claim that special realizations such as Hessian-eigenvector lines lose it. No higher dimension or inexact search is verified.
